focus: How is board quality measured today across references/quality-rubric.md and the manual-testing-playbook scorecard, and what would measure it better?
answeredQuestions: How is board quality measured today across references/quality-rubric.md and the manual-testing-playbook scorecard, and what would measure it better?

label: The scorecard measures what a machine can prove and what a stranger can answer - fidelity counts, reply shape, node immobility, three content questions - and the whole question of whether the board has a beginning, a grouping and a breathing rhythm falls between those two ends with no dimension asking it.

Clarity's three questions are content questions answerable by scanning labels in any order, so a reader can score three of three on a board whose first glance is a footnote - exactly the failure the corpus two-zoom overview pass exists to catch.

Layout conflates three different failures - a crossing, a shared trunk that makes edge ownership ambiguous, and a label sitting on its stroke - into one counter with three bands, where the corpus separates them and requires crossings to be judged from the rendered screenshot because a bounding box does not describe a path.

An unexamined dimension scores a silent 2 and a scored dimension carries no location, while the review contract the packet borrows from demands a location, the offending value, the fix and a criterion per finding plus an explicit zero per tier - so Layout 1 cannot be repaired without re-deriving the whole review.

Hygiene packs four independent invariants (no node moved, no extension covering a label, nothing outside the write changed, nothing written to export) into one bit, so one broken clause hides the other three and the report cannot say which failed.

Every scenario screenshots at 100% zoom only, so the overview judgment - if the first, second and last glance differ from the plan, revise scale, position, contrast or grouping - can never be made, and the author is always standing too close to notice that the first glance landed on a legend.

No scored reference board is kept, so a 12 of 14 has no meaning beyond one reviewer's opinion and scores are not comparable across sessions, types or releases; the design comparator keeps a dated benchmark report per run precisely so a regression is a diff rather than an opinion.

Several board qualities are computable from the parse the checker already performs - it returns profile, size and direction while counting nodes, connectors, participants, messages, entities, tasks and sections - so rank width, fan-out, edges per node, longest path, label-character load and a must-cross edge-pair estimate are cheap additions rather than a new machine.

The playbook records a scorecard verdict per session but keeps no series, so nobody can say whether board quality is rising; the comparator's dated benchmark folder with a results file and a findings file is the shape to copy.

The scorecard's pass condition - a total floor of 12 of 14, three dimensions held at 2, no dimension at 0 - is the right shape and should survive any redesign; what it lacks is a mandatory dimension covering composition, the one thing a reader notices before any count.

direction: Add a floating-point composite quality score
reason: A decimal built from seven judgements reads as precision the evidence cannot support; the floor-plus-mandatory-dimensions shape is more honest.

direction: Make flow_check.py score the board itself
reason: The checker sees Mermaid text; computed measures belong pre-write and reader measures belong in the playbook.

direction: Score every dimension with the same effort
reason: Fidelity and Reply are cheap and mechanical while the glance-order test needs a fresh reader; the scorecard should mark which dimensions are machine-checked.
